newsitem.title: USA: White House proposes bill to protect U.S. pensions.
newsitem.headline: White House proposes bill to protect U.S. pensions.

text.p: The Clinton administration Tuesday sent Congress proposed legislation to protect nearly 23 million pension programmes by making financial audits more comprehensive and accurate.

The legislation would also protect the retirement savings of Americans by requiring pension administrators to promptly report to the U.S. Labour Department "egregious violations of law affecting the integrity of benefit plans."
The department said the legislation would also save plans nationwide an estimated $2.5 million by eliminating an unnecessary filing requirement.

The draft bill was part of a national campaign initiated in October 1996 to crack down on pension fraud and abuse and followed the arrest last month of six individuals in cases involving total losses of more than $1 million.
Federal law requires pension plans with 100 or more participants receive an annual financial audit, but plan assets held by financial institutions may be excluded from the scope of the audit.
Currently about half of the 65,000 larger plans -- with assets totalling $950 billion -- were not receiving a meaningful audit due to this "limited scope audit" option.

The administration's proposed legislation would repeal this limited audit and ensure that "the financial operation of larger plans are more fully exposed to the sunlight of an audit," Labour Secretary Alexis Herman said in a statement.
The legislation would also expand the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corp.'s programme to locate missing pension beneficiaries and increase funding limits for contributions to multiemployer pension plans.
It would also provide additional retirement income protections for surviving spouses of federal workers under the Civil Service Retirement System.

The Labour and Justice departments have been cracking down on pension fraud, including misuse of employee contributions to 401K plans. To date the Labour Department has recovered more thanr $24 million for more than 40,000 workers nationwide.
